reply_text:
I found no dated AI prediction by Mustafa Suleyman from 2014. I ran the three fixed searches exactly as written, each once, and then eight more searches on 2014 occasions: talks, interviews, Wired, the Guardian and Financial Times, the DeepMind ethics board, and podcasts and panels. None of them turned up a page with his own forward-looking words from 2014. The results were mostly about the January 2014 Google deal for DeepMind (a reported $400–650 million) and his much later statements from 2016 to 2026. I used 11 of the 12 searches and 1 of the 6 page openings.

**What I read for this year:** the only page I opened was an essay he co-wrote with Demis Hassabis and Shane Legg. It answers Edge.org's question for **2015**, "What do you think about machines that think?", so it doesn't count for 2014. It says human-level AI is not "just around the corner" ("It's not"). It also says the remaining problems "can be overcome, but that it will take a generation of talented researchers equipped with plentiful computational resources". That's a timed prediction from 2015, and the essay was written jointly rather than by him alone, so I've put it under other_years. One limit: the page shows only the year 2015, not the exact day it was published.

**Not checked:** a US patent search result mentioned something Suleyman said in an interview, but I didn't open it and don't know the date, so it's not listed. I also didn't open the Financial Times piece from 27 January 2014, "DeepMind buy heralds rise of the machines", which appears in a Wikipedia reference list. It's the most likely place for 2014 words, but I couldn't confirm it quotes him.
